message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus zebra) belong to two very different orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively.  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore not a modern animal but an early **placental mammal** that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago, during the late Paleocene/early Eocene.  

That ancestor would have been a small, probably insect‑eating mammal that gave rise to the two lineages that eventually split into the diverse groups of carnivores (cats, dogs, bears, etc.) and odd‑toed ungulates (horses, zebras, rhinos, tapirs). In other words, the last common ancestor of lions and zebras is a primitive placental mammal that predates the divergence of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want the common ancestor of lion and zebra. We need to answer. The lion is a big cat (Panthera leo), zebra is a horse family (Equus zebra). They belong to different orders: lions are Carnivora, zebras are Perissodactyla. Their common ancestor would be a mammal from the clade Eutheria, maybe the last common ancestor of all placental mammals. But maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species, which is the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae. That would be a mammal from the order of early placentals. The last common ancestor of the two species is likely a small mammal from the Paleocene or early Eocene. But we can say: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras is a mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago, belonging to the group of early placental mammals. Or we can say: The common ancestor is a mammal from the clade of early placental mammals, possibly a small, insectivorous mammal. But maybe they want the common ancestor of the two species: the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae is a mammal from the order of early placental mammals, likely a small, omnivorous mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago. Or we can say: The common ancestor is a mammal from the clade of early placental mammals, possibly a small, insectivorous mammal. But we can also mention that the last common ancestor of all placental mammals is the ancestor of the group Eutheria, which existed around 100 million years ago. So the answer: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras is a small, early placental mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago, before the divergence of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla. Or we can say: The common ancestor is a mammal from the clade of early placental mammals, likely a small, insectivorous mammal. So answer accordingly.
